property_summary: The `oracle()` getter must return the address stored during construction; the mutant returns a hard-coded zero address instead.
The oracle() getter must return the address stored in contract storage; the mutant returns a fixed zero address, violating this rule for any initialized oracle.

The oracle() getter must return the address that was set during initialization; the mutant returns a hardcoded zero address, violating this rule for any non-zero oracle address provided in ProductInfo.

The oracle() getter must return the address that was set during initialization; the mutant returns a hardcoded zero address, violating this rule for any non-zero oracle address provided in ProductInfo.

The oracle() getter must return the address that was set during initialization; the mutant returns a hardcoded zero address, violating this rule for any non-zero oracle address provided in ProductInfo.

The oracle() getter must always return the oracle address that was set during initialization; the mutant breaks this by returning a hardcoded wrong address, so the returned value differs from the originally configured oracle.

The oracle() getter must return a contract address that responds to currentVersion() without reverting; the mutant returns address(0x...01) which is not a contract, causing currentVersion() to revert when called on the returned oracle.

The oracle() getter must return the address that was provided during the product's initialization; the mutant returns a hardcoded wrong address, so comparing it to the originally initialized oracle address exposes the bug.
When calling currentVersion() on the IOracleProvider returned by oracle(), the call must not revert (property of correct C), but the mutant's hardcoded non-contract address causes a revert.

For any product that was successfully initialized via its public initialize() function, calling c.oracle() must return the same address that was originally passed in the ProductInfo (preimage) during that initialization; the mutant returns a hardcoded different address, breaking the equality.

For any non-zero oracle version, the payoffDefinition returned by the reference contract always equals the originally stored definition; the mutant returns a definition with a potentially different payoffType, violating this invariant.

For any input, the payoffDefinition() return value should always equal the originally stored definition; the mutant forces payoffType to PASSTHROUGH, so the returned struct differs from the stored one.

The return value of payoffDefinition() must match the originally stored struct (including payoffType); the mutant forces payoffType to PASSTHROUGH, so if the stored type is not PASSTHROUGH, the return values differ.

For any call to payoffDefinition(), the returned PayoffDefinition struct must match the originally stored struct in all fields; the mutant forces payoffType to PASSTHROUGH, breaking equality when the stored type is different.

For any valid payoff definition initialization, the payoffType returned by payoffDefinition() must not be forcibly overridden to PASSTHROUGH; the bug sets it to PASSTHROUGH, changing the returned struct when the stored type differs.

For any initialized contract, payoffDefinition() must return the same payoff definition data that was originally set in storage; the mutant always zeroes out the data field, so returned data differs for any non-zero original data.
payoffDefinition().data must equal keccak256(abi.encode('EQUILIBRIA_PAYOFF_DEFINITION_STORAGE')) after initialization; the mutant always returns bytes30(0).
After initialization with a non-zero PayoffDefinition data, payoffDefinition().data must return the originally stored value; the mutant always returns bytes30(0), breaking equality.
The data field of the PayoffDefinition returned by payoffDefinition() should equal the data stored in storage; the mutant always zeroes it, so for any non‑zero stored data, the returned data differs.

The payoffDefinition() view function must return the exact PayoffDefinition stored in the contract's storage, including the original data field; the mutant zeroes out the data field, so for any non-zero stored data the returned struct differs.

For any initialization state, the payoffDirection returned by payoffDefinition() must match the stored definition's direction; the mutant always flips it, so retrieved direction never equals the stored one.

For any PayoffDefinition stored in the contract, the payoffDirection of the returned struct from payoffDefinition() must equal the payoffDirection of the internally stored definition; the mutant always returns a flipped direction, causing a mismatch even for the default/LONG case.

For any PayoffDefinition stored on the contract, the payoffDirection returned by payoffDefinition() must equal the original direction of the definition at initialization; the mutant flips the direction for LONG/SHORT, so the returned direction will be the opposite of what was originally set.

For any initialized PayoffDefinition, the payoffDirection returned by payoffDefinition() must equal the direction of the PayoffDefinition originally passed to initialize; the mutant flips the direction for LONG/SHORT, so the returned direction will differ from the originally set one.

For any initialized contract, the payoffType of the PayoffDefinition returned by payoffDefinition() must equal the payoffType of the stored PayoffDefinition; the mutant, while flipping payoffDirection, must not alter payoffType, ensuring equality holds in the reference but can be falsified by the mutant depending on the fuzzed payoffType due to a possible side-effect of the flip logic.
The price in currentVersion() must equal the payoff transformation of the oracle price; the buggy version returns the raw untransformed oracle price instead.
